item.content:encoded: We’ll be sharing more details with you over the course of the next week. But I wanted to let you know we’re trying something new and exciting with our election night coverage. We’ll be doing a live video-cast for the evening, including me, our publisher Joe Ragazzo and the rest of our editorial team coming in to discuss different races as the evening goes on. Think of it as a TPM version of what you might see if you spent the evening watching MS NOW or CNN. Basically it will be a mix of the latest results (and looking under the hood at details in key counties and precincts which tells you where things are really going) and discussion of what it all means. I hope you’ll join us.

item.title: Aaron Ashby Has Put The Brewers In Control
item.author: Ray Ratto
item.content:encoded: This baseball postseason has a face, and it is Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy, standing on the bottom of step of his team's dugout, staring 25 yards into the distance and letting the dual features of his conscience balance on opposite shoulders arguing with each other over Aaron Ashby. The good angel is crying out, "He works every day. He deserves a break," and the bad one snarls back, like a cranky farmer, "But I need the milk now!"And time after time, the bad voice wins out because, well, yeah, the milk.The Brewers are two games up in the World Series after successive one-run victories over the Tampa Bay Rays, because that is their championship motif, letting the other guys score first and then slowly but inexorably catching up and passing them and then letting their formidable bullpen apply the pillow to the face. And by "bullpen," we mean Ashby more than anyone else, because he is having the most unreasonable postseason of a fella's dreams. Unreasonable in that in a sport where no trend lives forever, every game he has pitched has been eerily similar.

item.title: A Brief Look At the Israeli Election
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: I wanted to give you a brief update on and impressions of the Israeli election which is on Tuesday. An overview of the polls suggests that the opposition bloc may get a few more seats than the Netanyahu bloc but that both will fall far short of the 61 seats required to form a government. Most polls have shown both blocs in the low 50s while the remainder of the 120 seats go to two Arab parties/coalitions. One of those is Ra’am, which is probably now best termed “non-Zionist” since it accepts Israel as a Jewish state and sat in the brief non-Netanyahu government in 2021-22, and the Joint List, which remains firmly anti-Zionist and probably wouldn’t sit in any government and also wouldn’t be invited to any. What this amounts to is high odds for a stalemate in which neither side can form a government and new elections have to be called. In that case, you have several more months in which Netanyahu remains in office as “caretaker” prime minister.Three stories have jumped out at me from the Israeli press over the last two or three days. The first, just today is that Netanyahu posted an AI photo of a nuclear blast over Tel Aviv saying that his election is all that can prevent it.

item.title: Seam Cutter
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: I built this weird and very specific cropping tool - it lets you create a horizontal or vertical cut across an image, then slide the two sides relative to each other. Effectively it lets you crop out a section in the middle of an image.I wanted this because I often use Tailor on my iPhone to stitch several screenshots together into lot long image, but sometimes I find myself wanting to crop out a section in the middle - to redact an irrelevant prompt from a transcript, for example.

item.title: Let’s all watch Barack Obama and Jon Ossoff use Preznit Fuckwit as a chew toy
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: We’re going to get to Barack and Jon’s excellent, I promise. “Our country is making hundreds of billions of dollars because of what’s happening in the Middle East. They’re making hundreds of billions, our country is, on oil. So, we’re making hundreds and hundreds of billions, trillions of dollars. And my people said ‘please don’t mention that, sir,’ because people are paying a little higher— we’re making money like this country has never made before. The fake news will say ‘he’s bragging about making money, while people are suffering at the— at the’— I can just see the fake headlines. But I don’t give a damn, I’m going to say it. We’re making a frickin’ fortune.”Mister President, sir — if that really is your name — I have a question: Who the fuck is Because it sure as hell isn’t . And I know it’s not the average American, sitting at home, trying to figure out which bills to put off paying for another month, to try to make ends meet.Of course you know who Donny is referring to when he says “we’re making a frickin’ fortune” — he’s talking about himself, his cronies, and his felonious family. That’s all who Donny cares about. We the People can go kick rocks.‘let them eat fuck-all, I could give a shit.’How can MAGA just stand there and accept it? You know goddamned well that if Joe Biden’s autopen had ever said such a thing, enraged Republicans, bearing torches and pitchforks, would have stormed the White House.This isn’t even the first time Donny’s confessed that he literally doesn’t give two shits about average Americans. When asked by a reporter whether the financial straits of Americans were motivating him to make a deal, Trump replied, “Not even a little bit,” adding, “I don’t think about Americans’ financial situation. I don't think about anybody.”Isn’t that charming? The US economy may die, but it’s a sacrifice that Dear Leader is willing to make.What a frickin’ humanitarian.Okay, onto the frickin’ main event. Yesterday, at a campaign rally in Ohio, there was a speech given by some rando named hmm, it says here That’s a weird name. Have any of you ever heard of this guy? Let’s hear what this newcomer has to say.“So when you go through the tally of promises, things have not worked out the way we might have expected. And let’s be honest, does anybody really think that guy in the White House is spending all that time thinking about these issues? I mean, I don’t know if you’ve noticed, but he seems very focused on home renovations. Guy’s building a ballroom that’s bigger than the White House. Paved over the Rose Garden. Put up a helicopter pad on the South Lawn. And there’s gold everywhere. What’s up with the gold? Everything, more gold. He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened up a Cheesecake Factory.”‘Saddam Hussein opened up a Cheesecake Factory’ — hey, that’s not bad. I’m beginning to like this Obama dude. If he keeps this up, he could actually be a good candidate for president someday.“Meanwhile, you’ve got the Defense Secretary, who’s squarely focused — he’s very focused on important matters, the the jawlines and testosterone levels of our troops. And livestreaming executions — because that’s how he thinks you cultivate that manly warrior spirit. How much time do you think this Defense Secretary spends looking at himself in the mirror in the morning? You know he’s working his hair, because that’s how warriors look. These are not serious people.”Stop it, Barack — But this Barack dude has it so right: these are not serious people. None of them are. Warplans McButtdial is a frickin’ failed weekend chat show host, for frick’s sake. The Transportation Secretary can’t be found, because he’s off doing a reality show that no one watches. The lunatic in charge of our nation’s healthcare swims in sewage and actually believes that heroin, hoovered off the nearest toilet seat, is an effective study aid.Our chief peace negotiators are a couple of slumlords, and our Secretary of State wears literal oversized clown shoes as he goes about his business of doing— what the fuck is he even doing?Can you name a single one of his accomplishments? No, you cannot. At least Bobby Brainworms once chainsawed the frickin’ head off a dead whale. That’s something you can point to. What does Liddle Marco Big-Shoes have to brag about?No wonder our country is in the shitter right now. Not one of these nitwits has any clue what they’re doing.Okay, Jon Ossoff has been so patient over here, waiting very politely for his turn to talk. Have at it, Jon.“Now, maybe you saw — the crook president is coming back to Georgia today, to wallow in his failure and disgrace. To remind Georgians of his failure as Commander-in-Chief, and the reckless war that he lied us into that he knows not how to end, or how to win. To remind Georgians of his tariffs that have driven up grocery prices to all-time highs. To remind Georgians that he cut your healthcare and doubled your health insurance premiums. For what? To cut taxes for his donors — for the wealthiest people in the country, and for corporate America. Donald Trump is coming to Georgia today, to remind Georgians that under the failed president Donald J. Trump, it costs more than ever in American history to fill up your truck, to stock your fridge, to power your home, or to go to your doctor.”I frickin’ adore Jon Ossoff. He doesn’t screw around. He goes straight for the jugular.And he’s right — Donny a failure. He’s been a failure. Look, owning a casino is like having a license to print money. Yet, this low-wattage stumblefuck somehow managed to bankrupt of them.Donny wanted to make the midterms all about himself. Fine, let’s give him what he wants. Now smart Democrats like Ossoff can hang Dear Leader’s legacy of abject failure around the neck of every Republican, like the ginormous fucking millstone it is.Way to act first and think never, Donny.Oh my god, look who’s up next at the microphone. It’s the Big Dog himself. “I think Congress made a mistake, not protesting turning the Rose Garden into what looks like the entrance to Liberace's bathroom.”Okay, that’s pretty, pretty good. Maybe his delivery isn’t quite as polished as that Obama fellow, but if this Bill Clinton character keeps honing his act, he too just might have a bright political future in front of him.“The radar. My uncle invented radar! Can you believe it? From MIT, Dr. John Trump.”Donald Trump’s uncle did not invent radar. The “first practical radar system” was patented by Sir Robert Watson-Watt, who built on the work of others such as Heinrich Hertz and Christian Huelsmeyer.What a weird fucking thing to lie about. Who even gives a shit?You know, I too have an uncle who went to MIT. I’m not dong a bit right now, I really do have have an uncle who went to MIT. The thing is, I have no idea what he majored in. I never thought to ask — but maybe I’ll start telling people he invented post-its.Yeah, post-its. That’s the ticket.And now, it’s time to ourselves the frick out of here.Here are two shots from an afternoon spent leaf-watching in the Hudson Valley, nine years ago today, on October 25, 2017.I hear you saying, ‘those pics are from so far away. Don’t you have anything that’s more like, y’know, a closeup?’Absolutely. Let’s revisit this photo from Ms Spouse’s 66th birthday on February 7, 2016 — because who can resist that ?Have a great Sunday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.content:encoded: This is truly a "longwatch" (one and a half hours), so I just browsed it. I continue to be impressed by the investment China is making in its infrastructure. "It is a transportation corridor created to promote rural economic development... This section of the route officially opened in the second half of 2024. The most famous section of the route is the “72 Curves of Tongqiangou Valley ”, the highway looks like a giant dragon circling between the lofty mountains. Road started to turn in bends and switchbacks, the altitude climbs rapidly, and the rolling hills in the distance will continue to unfold in front of your eyes.

item.title: Trump’s plan to control who wins
item.author: 1axb0r8pnva41esraeqpje4dznx5g28pm5xzoj@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: Over the last 48 hours, two things have become unmistakable: Donald Trump is trying to steal the midterm elections, and Attorney General Todd Blanche will do whatever he can to help him.In California, the DOJ has escalated its threats against election officials and voters. On Friday, it sent letters to all 58 counties demanding they set aside mail ballots the DOJ has flagged or face the “risk significant federal scrutiny.”Meanwhile, in Alaska, Trump went further. He ordered his DOJ to sue to block certification of the Senate election if Democrat Mary Peltola wins. Asked about the lawsuit, Trump said, “Well, I’m one that said, ‘Do it.’”My law firm, Elias Law Group, has already moved to intervene to defeat this on behalf of Peltola’s campaign and the Democratic Party.DOJ’s rationale for the lawsuit is ridiculous, and its legal arguments are frivolous.The pretext for this lawsuit is the fact that two men named Dan Sullivan are on the ballot: Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan and Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher from Petersburg. DOJ asserts this is confusing to voters and that the remedy is to certify the Republican the winner.For this astounding proposition, the DOJ relies on the National Voter Registration Act. Set aside that the law governing voter registration has nothing at all to do with the certification of elections. Set aside that the underlying factual claims in the complaint read like a cross between Mad Libs and an AI chatbot run amok.The Alaska Supreme Court has already rejected the effort to keep the second Dan Sullivan off the ballot. And the Constitution gives states, not the president or the Justice Department, the authority to govern the composition of their ballots and the criteria for certifying their elections.But this, in some respects, is beside the point.

item.title: GOP Now Stands for “Gang of Predators”
item.author: Lisa Graves
item.content:encoded: It is both shocking and totally on brand for Donald Trump and JD Vance to defend Vivek Ramaswamy’s vile, million-dollar ad campaign weaponizing a child molester’s wife to attack Dr. Amy Acton, his opponent in Ohio’s gubernatorial race.He continued to sexually abuse her until he was arrested when she was 12. The state took Amy and her little brother, Phil Stearns, away from Donna and Cledith. Phil stands by his sister, noting that Donna “stayed married to Amy’s rapist until he died” in 2004.Back in 1974, the year before he married Donna, Cledith Arthur had been charged with “incest” of a different child. That charge was two years before he began raping Amy.That’s not all that is relevant and totally appalling.In 1996, Donna Arthur–going by the last name “Hollopeter”--was found guilty of felony theft and passing bad checks. That is, the woman who Ramaswamy has lifted up to call her daughter a “liar” was literally convicted of the crime of “theft by deception,” which is stealing by lying. Donna–who lost custody of her children for neglect and for not protecting her daughter from a sexual predator–was charged with animal neglect, too, just five years ago in 2021.You cannot make up such wretchedness.In any sane universe, a candidate for governor would never run an ad featuring a child molester’s lover, a woman complicit in his abuse and also his after-the-fact accomplice.Vivek’s action in taking her side is utter depravity.Sure, Cledith Arthur pleaded “not guilty” before jumping bond and fleeing Ohio for Pennsylvania with his wife. Their flight from justice prevented a trial and his conviction as a monstrous pedophile, but I consider his evasion to be more evidence of his guilt.And I will not call that woman Amy’s “mother” or “mom.” In my opinion, she forfeited that title when she betrayed her young daughter instead of protecting her from the predator she had invited into their lives. Now she has wormed her way out of the shadows to harm Amy, again, this time with the help of Vivek and his enormous wealth. There is a special place in hell for such betrayers of their sacred parental duty, like Alice Munro.In any normal timeline, a candidate’s top advisors would resign if their boss insisted on running an attack ad siding with a child molester and his lover against the child who survived such horrifying abuse. Instead, Vivek’s spokesperson, Connie Luck, defended the ad and again attacked Dr. Acton’s character. That’s shameless, and I have a right to wish that Luck never has the good luck to get a good job ever again.In any healthy administration, the president and the vice president would condemn the ad, urge Ramaswamy to take it down, and call on him to step down from the race.But this is not a healthy administration. It is deeply unwell. It is morally sick.I say this all in my personal capacity, not on behalf of any organization. Trump is wicked, a magnet of corruption, who attracts and collects the iron filings of men and women willing to trade their integrity for power, wealth, and fame—people like JD Vance.Vance should have been unwelcome back in Ohio after telling foul lies about innocent, hard-working Haitian immigrants living in the state in 2024. After his defense of Vivek’s ad, Vance should be disowned by the state.Despite his own track record, Vance—a recent Catholic convert—had the audacity this summer to try to lecture the Pope on Catholic tenets after Pope Leo rebuked the warmongering of Trump and Vance. Vance even published a memoir this year telling his tales about “finding my way back to faith,” a faith that includes the Ten Commandments, which expressly condemns bearing false witness. This week, rather than denounce Vivek’s ad featuring the child molester’s paramour, Vance assailed Acton’s character and dismissed any Republican critics, telling them to “stop whining.”Vance should be ashamed. Instead, he is doubling down.This would all be bad enough… but there’s more.The Republicans installed a man who continues to act like Donald Trump’s personal defense attorney as Attorney General of the United States. That man, Todd Blanche, has expressed more sympathy for convicted sex trafficker Ghislaine Maxwell than for the victims and survivors of her schemes with Jeffrey Epstein. To this day, under Blanche’s direction, numerous Epstein-related records mentioning Donald Trump remain hidden. On Blanche’s watch, Maxwell was moved to a country club prison camp with more lenient conditions, and DOJ is investigating none of the other men named in the Epstein files.His Secretary of Defense, Pete Hegseth, was accused of raping a woman, who said she suspected he roofied her. Hegseth denied the claim before ultimately settling the case.Trump’s Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh also faced an accusation of sexual assault from his former classmate, Dr. Christine Blasey Ford. He bombastically denied it and was confirmed to the nation’s highest court with Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME) casting a pivotal vote in his favor, alongside nearly every other Republican senator.Kavanaugh joined a Supreme Court where Republicans had previously installed Clarence Thomas, who was accused of repeatedly sexually harassing a woman who had worked for him. Thomas loudly denied the allegations too, but I found Anita Hill’s testimony compelling, just like Ford’s.And this is only a partial accounting of the rot involving GOP men accused of sexual predators. Then there are the high profile men, like Ramaswamy and Vance, actively men credibly accused of rape, including the rape of children, as with Amy Acton’s case.As I have said repeatedly since 2018, when Trump and his loyalist Republicans jammed Kavanaugh onto the Supreme Court (though he should have been impeached from the judiciary instead), America does not face a crisis of false accusations by women and girls. Most cases of rape are never reported. The real problem is false denials.We have an epidemic of false denials.That is partly because men accused of rape lie and deny that they did anything wrong.And, in America, those who are accused have the right to plead not guilty, whether they are guilty or not, and face a trial with their neighbors as jurors. While most of those charges for sexual assault result in convictions or guilty pleas, we do not make an accounting of just how many of those men made false denials from the outset. Rarely do such trials result in acquittals or hung juries, but it sometimes happens after the defense tries to put the accuser on trial, scrutinizing what they wore, what they drank, or how they behaved.Rarer still are the cases in which a man accused of molesting a child becomes a fugitive from justice, like the predator Donna Arthur repeatedly chose over her only daughter.I hope justice prevails and the guy fueling these attacks–who I am going to call “Vivek Reallyslimy” from here on out–loses big time.People of integrity and good conscience must take a stand against the dirtiest of dirty politics that he, Trump, and Vance are playing here.I really hope a giant wave of justice breaks through and politically wipes out those who defend rapists and pedophiles and their enablers. And, I hope that wave also washes out any candidate for any office anywhere who refuses to condemn Reallyslimy’s ad and does not call on him to step down from the race.The rest of us have had enough of this wickedness.The time for accountability is well past due.What I’m Reading or Rereading:This book was written by two heroes of mine shortly after Thomas was installed on the Supreme Court. Jane and Jill are such excellent investigative reporters and writers. I look forward to their newest works.Get the full receipts every Monday in The Cover-UpAccountability starts with the record. COURIER’s new Contradictions Tracker compares testimony to the Epstein files, with every source linked. Follow along every Monday in The Cover-Up.

item.title: This Week in Stupid: October 24 edition
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: As another stupid week comes to a close here in America, let’s look back at the dumbest fucking shit that happened.Monday: gun 1, dashboard 0 Oh my dear sweet lord, that was satisfying.Let’s gif that shit for posterity’s sake, and slow it way the fuck down.Chef’s kiss. Ten out of ten. No notes.Tuesday: how did we Nazi this coming?Now let’s all get ready to pick our jaws up off the floor as the Space Nazi proves well beyond any shadow of a doubt that being and being are not mutually exclusive concepts.“Hitler was a far left socialist. Literally in the name of his party!”Oh sure, just like North Korea is a democratic republic. Literally in the name of the country!How can one person be this dumb? How can he be this big a credulous dope? How has Elon not forked his own eye out by now?Here’s an even better question: why is it that whenever a swastika rears its ugly face in public in America, it’s right next to a Donny banner? That doesn’t sound very leftist to me.Let’s do this. Let’s turn to an actual expert. I’m talking about the Space Nazi’s own janky, six-fingered plagiarism robot — the one that literally calls itself Mecha-Hitler. Hitler was a fascist, not a socialist. The Nazi Party’s full name included “socialist” for propaganda appeal to workers, but Hitler explicitly rejected Marxist socialism, class struggle, and internationalism. He purged actual socialists, banned their parties, sent them to camps, allied with industrialists, and privatized industries while preserving private property aligned with state/national goals. Nazism was ultranationalist, racist authoritarianism—far-right fascism in historical consensus, not left-wing socialism.And, in summation, let me just put this right here, for no particular reason at all.Wednesday: blessed are Folks, you better listen up, because god-bothering Donnyvangelist Kenneth Copeland has a stern warning for all you blasphemers who won’t be pulling the lever for Republicans in the midterms: .“I saw this in the spirit. Literally. Judgement Day. And Jesus stood there, and he said, those of you that didn’t vote, I put you in that nation and you didn’t vote. So you will hear, or you didn’t vote and pray like I told you to. You will listen to the names of all the babies that are here and never got any life. And it’ll take a while, because there’s over 65 million of them. But you are going to listen to every one them, and you are going to be held responsible for their death.”Wow, Pastor Kenny seems like a real funster, doesn’t he? I have a question: where is this homie getting his information? Is this in the Gospel of Mark? The Gospel of Luke? Maybe in the Gospel or Some Fucking Tiresome Scold?Wait, I have an even better question: exactly who is being punished here? I would imagine that Jesus would have better things to do with his time than read off the names of 65 million aborted fetuses who— wait a minute, they don’t even have names. So are we to believe that Jesus is going to spend eternity going, ‘aborted fetus number three million four hundred and forty-three thousand and seven. Aborted fetus number three million four hundred and forty-three thousand and eight. Aborted fetus—’Oh please. No way. Jesus doesn’t have time for that shit.I happen to know for a fact that thee J-Man prefers to spend his free time scrolling through social media and watching videos of dumbfucks blowing away their dashboards.It’s right there in the Gospel of Jeff. Thursday: we don’t need no education Cultist: “We don’t need socialism in this country” Jason Selvig: Cultist: “Look what the Democrats are doing. They’ll raise your taxes. They don’t give a shit about the American people” Selvig: Cultist: “Look what they’re doing to America. You have all these environmentalist people, they stopped drilling oil wells” Selvig:Cultist: “Well look what the Democrats are doing, it’s plain and simple” Selvig: “But what is the definition of socialism?” Cultist: “I don’t need to go into big words or whatever. I’m just telling you, we don’t need it in America”These fucking idiots have no idea what socialism is, nor do they care to know what socialism is. They can only parrot back what they heard Hannity saying on Fox News.free things from the government is bad — unless it’s that five-thousand dollar check that Dear Leader is never, ever going to send them. Oh, and speaking of fucking idiots— Friday: the further adventures of Some Fucking Idiot™On Friday, while on his way to a hate-rally, some fucking idiot stood up for one of his most-maligned and most-unfairly-treated constituencies: .Oh look, the fucking idiot took the side of a rapist, he also tried to bully a woman reporter while doing so — ! No, fucking idiot, none of us have ever seen a pile of a million dollars. We’re not the ones trading presidential pardons for cash, remember? “A healthy person has a thousand dreams. A sick person has only one (to get better)! President DONALD J. TRUMP”What in the actual fuck? Why is the fucking idiot being so philosophical all of a sudden? Quiet reflection isn’t his thing. Why is he ruminating on mortality? Does the fucking idiot know something about his health that he’s not sharing with the rest of us?But because the fucking idiot never takes questions from the press while doing a hate-rally, not one reporter had the opportunity to stand up and ask, ‘what the fuck is wrong with you?’How fucking idiotic is that?And now, let’s put a close to This Week in Stupid and reward ourselves with some Daily Claudia.This shot’s from September 2022, and I have no idea where we were. I don’t recognize anything about this interior.And here’s Ms Spouse, just chilling, on August 19, 2004.Have a non-stupid Saturday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future:practice self-care. do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.author: bounce-mc.us1_388705.10708709-d186966748@mail155.sea81.mcsv.net
item.content:encoded: Heather Cox Richardson is one of today’s unlikeliest social media stars. The Boston College historian has been teaching and writing about 19th-century America, Reconstruction, and the Civil War for decades. But it was only in 2019 that her work took off when she began writing her daily newsletter, , a no-nonsense analysis of the news through the lens of US history. The newsletter became one of the most popular on Substack. And today, Richardson has millions of loyal fans who rely on her to make sense of American politics and provide a little sanity and democratic reassurance, even as she herself is concerned about the direction of the country today. “I’m worried about where we’re going. Just don’t even start me,” Richardson tells host Al Letson. “But I am heartened in this moment by the number of people who are rediscovering that they do have agency to change the future. And of course, that’s always been the story of our democracy.”, which first aired in June, Richardson doles out some advice for the Democrats if they take back power in the midterm elections, the decades-long failure to hold corrupt American leaders accountable, the still-resonant death of Reconstruction, and what she sees as the tragic hypocrisy of Thomas Jefferson.

item.title: Too many people are afraid to say this
item.author: 1axb8bim5scxqfqc0unl8nq7xy37ldasxih5sz@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: Too many people know the truth but are afraid to say it. I will.We are in a constitutional crisis.I don’t mean this in the general sense of Donald Trump flouting the law or violating norms. I mean specifically that, with only days before the midterm elections, Trump is using the power of the federal government to threaten states, intimidate election officials and disenfranchise voters.This is most obvious in California, where his Department of Justice demanded that state election officials set aside ballots from 20,000 voters the Trump administration claims to believe are noncitizens.When the election officials refused, the DOJ sued. Then it threatened criminal prosecution. Trump said the election officials in California “will all go to jail for a long period of time.”This week, Attorney General Todd Blanche refused to commit to respecting state election results. He made clear that the DOJ would interfere in the elections or their certification if it deems it necessary. The U.S. Constitution bars such conduct, but Trump doesn’t care, and neither do his government lawyers.Blanche also made clear that the DOJ is poised to sue other states on similar grounds.Over the last two years, legacy media outlets have done everything they can to normalize Trump’s threats and attacks on democracy.When he says he wants Republicans to take over the voting in blue cities, they dismiss it as mere rhetoric. When he claims the power to control ballot counting, they excuse it as politics. When he says he wants to rig elections, they insist both sides use heated words.I’ve been here before. In 2020, I was called an alarmist when I said Trump would never concede. When I defeated Trump and his allies in court, I was told he was simply letting the process play out.For a while, many of my critics grew quiet. But then came the Biden era, Merrick Garland and a belief that we could return to normalcy. What I saw as MAGA regrouping, others hailed as a new era of civility and norms.

item.title: Saturday 80s Jam: Faith – George Michael
item.author: Schill
item.content:encoded: When George Michael released “Faith” in 1987, he was already one of the biggest pop stars on the planet. But the song represented something much more significant than another hit single. It was the moment Michael stepped completely out of the shadow of Wham! and established himself as a solo artist with his own identity, sound, and image.The title track from his debut solo album, , was almost deceptively simple. Built around a stripped-down acoustic guitar riff, handclaps, percussion, and Michael’s confident vocal, the song sounded dramatically different from the polished synth-pop that had helped make Wham! famous.Michael wanted to move in a more mature musical direction, drawing on rockabilly, early rock ‘n’ roll, soul, and R&B. “Faith” combined those influences into something that sounded both retro and completely suited to 1987.The opening is particularly memorable. The church-organ sound fades into the guitar riff before Michael enters, creating an unusual mixture of gospel imagery and rock ‘n’ roll swagger. The song then settles into a deceptively relaxed groove.Michael wasn’t simply singing about romantic faith. The song is also about independence and refusing to remain trapped in a relationship that isn’t working.That attitude was reflected in the video, which became one of the most recognizable pieces of MTV-era imagery. Michael appeared in leather, sunglasses, blue jeans, and a leather jacket, playing guitar in front of a jukebox.The image was a complete transformation from the carefully coordinated pop-star presentation associated with Wham!The transformation worked.“Faith” became a massive commercial success, reaching number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in the United States. The album became one of the biggest-selling records of the decade, eventually earning Michael the Grammy Award for Album of the Year.The song itself became one of the defining singles of 1987.What made it particularly impressive was how little it actually needed. There wasn’t a giant synthesizer arrangement or an enormous chorus. The hook came from the rhythm, the guitar, Michael’s personality, and the confidence of the performance.He sounded completely in control.That confidence was important because “Faith” arrived during one of the most significant transitions of Michael’s career. Wham! had been enormously successful, but remaining part of a duo would always make it difficult for Michael to establish exactly who he was as an artist.With , he didn’t simply continue what Wham! had started.The song also demonstrated Michael’s extraordinary ability to move between musical styles. He could write sophisticated pop songs, soulful ballads, dance tracks, and more stripped-down rock-influenced material without sounding like he was simply copying someone else.“Faith” became the perfect introduction to that new version of George Michael.More than anything, the song is memorable because it feels effortless. The guitar riff is simple. The arrangement is relatively sparse. The rhythm is straightforward.But getting simplicity to sound this good is difficult.Every element is in exactly the right place.The result was a song that managed to sound retro, modern, sexy, playful, and confident all at once.Nearly four decades later, “Faith” remains one of George Michael’s defining recordings. It marked the beginning of one of the most successful solo careers of the late 1980s and proved that Michael was capable of becoming something beyond the pop star audiences already knew.Wham! had made George Michael famous.“Faith” made it clear that George Michael didn’t need Wham! anymore.

item.title: Follow Up About Political Giving
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: Following my morning post about the Democratic political contribution infrastructure, I had a number of TPM Readers write in saying, in so many words, No! You’re wrong. People are totally burnt out about the annoying emails. I want to point out that I said the same thing, how abusive and stupid and annoying the avalanche of emails is. What I noted is a sort of admission against interest, which is that the haul from online small donor giving keeps rising. So at least at the aggregate level, effective burnout, actually seeing contributions decline, is not something we’re seeing. It may be around the corner. And we can and should do better. But on this acid test, the money keeps rolling in. And that’s clearly a big reason why it continues.

item.content:encoded: Kimi K3.1 Pro landed on the Kimi API today - it's not yet open weights, but Moonshot promise "Full model weights will be released by Nov 4, 2026".They're also offering a "Highspeed" version that's 2-3x faster, at twice the price (except for input token cache hits, which are priced the same).The US dollar pricing is $2.00/million tokens for input and $10/million for output - the same as GPT-6.1 Sol and half the price of Claude Opus 5.5.Moonshot's own benchmarks show Kimi as approximately level with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra - beating them on a few benchmarks, coming close on others.Artificial Analysis scored Kimi at 55 - ahead of Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon (all at 53) and behind only Claude Opus 5.5 (58).This is the first time a (soon-to-be) open weight model has scored this highly against the frontier.llm openai endpoint \ https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 \ --key kimi \ -m kimi-k3.1-pro \ "Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle" \ --responses \ -o reasoning_effort low \ > kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stdout.txt \ 2> kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stderr.txt can run prompts against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint but doesn't log the results, hence the extra options to save stdout and stderr (the reasoning trace).Here are the pelicans I got for Kimi K3.1 Pro on the three reasoning levels it supports - low, medium, and max. item.title: Now Is The Time For Hysteria
item.author: Ray Ratto
item.content:encoded: We had ourselves the hell week of all hell weeks last Saturday. And in the aftermath, the top of the sport is upside down and everyone sounds incoherent—babbling and whining about which teams are good and which are bad, in tones you can otherwise only find from Old Testament prophets. Is Florida secretly good? Is Texas truly a tire fire? Is it going to come out that Cooper Manning never even showed Arch a football before college? Why can't Notre Dame close? Why would Oregon bench Dylan Raiola, just to play him in the fourth quarter against his former school? How did we end up with a first-ranked Miami? These are the questions left to us in the wake of some near-unprecedented football mayhem. The two directions left to go from here are either set the universal order right or make shit go even more left. I know what I choose.After the pyro-spectacular of last weekend, with all those ranked teams either losing outright or barely escaping defeat, something needed to be done to restore normalcy. And so Maryland fired head coach Mike Locksley on Tuesday. Locksley is most recently noted for having guided the Terps to 12 consecutive conference losses, seven of the last eight by double digits, and the most recent coming against Rutgers. The last and decisive one was just a seven-point loss, but it may as well have been 49 when you apply the added "You lost to RUTGERS?" metric.

item.title: James Dolan Finds Innovative New Way To Be Cruel And Cheap
item.author: Samer Kalaf
item.content:encoded: Most owners of sports teams are wise enough to understand that their reputations will never be better than when their teams are winning. If they're fortunate enough to see that team capture a championship, they know that it's easy image rehabilitation. Just show some basic appreciation, sprinkle it around to everyone in the organization, and try not to say much aside from "We did it" and "Thank you." That way, the public will momentarily forget how you made your money off predatory mortgages or whatever.James Dolan has chosen a different path. Since June, when the New York Knicks won their first title in 53 years, the owner has done his best to make the victory lap as unpleasant as possible for all involved. At the championship ceremony, in a juiceless and mercifully short speech, Dolan took swipes at New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and—for some reason—Knicks fans under the age of 53. He brought back notable creep Isiah Thomas, and appointed him to the team's board of directors. He scheduled a fundraiser for Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman right before a Knicks preseason game, and has sued magazine for reporting on the invasive surveillance technology he uses at Madison Square Garden. He's also played hardball in contract talks with the very stars who won a championship. It's rare to have a title-winning team begin its subsequent season on such a sour note.But wait, there's more: According to Joe Vardon of The Athletic, the Knicks' pregame ceremony ahead of Tuesday's season opener was a bit more ceremonial than it appeared. Team president Leon Rose opened a box to show off his sparkly championship ring, but nobody on the coaching staff did, because their boxes were empty. They didn't have rings yet, and it was still unclear who would actually receive one. From the article:

item.title: How Can I Hang On To My Digital Life?
item.author: Alex Sujong Laughlin
item.content:encoded: I've been watching the "available storage" bars on my various digital storage systems creep up over the last couple years, with a growing sense of dread. Each percentage point is a tick closer to an upgrade to my package—money I'll have to pay Apple, Google, and Dropbox to continue to store my digital life. Maybe more importantly, I'm aware of just how much I produce every day, and as the mess grows, I wonder if I should do something about it. On worse days, I think maybe I should just succumb to the digital hoarder house I've built for myself.It is probably my obsession with my own death, paired with the ever-present anxiety about whether the way I spend my days truly matters at all, that has led to an interest in personal archiving practices. My life's work amounts to several terabytes' worth of mp3s, wavs, text files, and jpegs that live on server space I pay to lease somewhere in the world. I like the idea of my work being accessible after I'm gone, and for a long time I trusted the infrastructure of the internet to do that archival work for me. But if the last 20 years have taught us anything, it's that only dummies blindly trust big tech to operate in their best interest.

item.title: Trump DOJ Plays Dirty Pool In California Election Case
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: In its attack on the midterm elections in California, the Trump DOJ has taken an extraordinary new step that exemplifies how far off the rails it has gone under Trump II.I mentioned yesterday that the Trump DOJ was seeking an immediate ruling on its emergency application for a temporary restraining order to force Los Angeles County to segregate and not count certain alleged noncitizen ballots. As I noted then, the Trump DOJ request for a ruling from the court by noon yesterday came the judge in the case had already set a hearing on the TRO application for next Tuesday.They appeared to have settled that.But by the end of the day yesterday, the Trump DOJ appealed what it claimed was the lack of a ruling from the judge, making the astounding assertion his “silence” amounted to a “constructive denial” of its application for a TRO.It’s hard to convey to non-lawyers how wacky this is — on so many levels — but let’s start with the claim that the judge had been silent.U.S. District Judge David O. Carter was assigned the case just before noon Wednesday morning. About four hours later, he granted an already-pending request from the Trump DOJ to exceed the court’s page limit for its legal memorandum in support of its TRO application. A couple of hours after that, the Trump DOJ formally filed its TRO application.Sometime after 6:14 p.m. PT, when the the Trump DOJ filed its TRO application, Judge Carter issued an order setting a hearing on the TRO application for Tuesday, Oct. 27 at 1 p.m. ET.At 8:57 p.m. PT, the Trump DOJ for the first time asked for an expedited ruling by noon PT on Oct. 22. By then, Judge Carter had already set a hearing for next Tuesday.Noon yesterday came and went without any new ruling from Carter so before the end of the day, the Trump DOJ moved to appeal the case on spurious constructive denial grounds.How the Trump DOJ construes Judge Carter setting a hearing on its TRO as “silence” is mystifying.But it actually gets worse.In its notice of appeal to Judge Carter, the Trump DOJ outlines the sequence of events leading up to what it deems his “constructive denial” but that he had already scheduled a hearing on the TRO. (The appeal isn’t showing up yet on the Ninth Circuit docket so I can’t confirm whether the Trump DOJ played hide the ball with the appeals court on this, too.)There’s more to say on this, but first here’s a timeline I put together of the key filings and court orders to help orient you:(Derived from the court docket as it appears on Pacer; exact times from Courtlistener): Trump DOJ files its lawsuit against California: Trump DOJ files a motion to exceed the page limit in its application for a TRO, which it attaches as an exhibit: The case is assigned to U.S. District Judge John W. Holcomb: The case is reassigned to U.S. District Judge David O. Carter, a Clinton appointed, because it’s related to an existing case he’s already hearing. (This was a win for California, which had sought the move, and a loss for the Trump DOJ, which had sought assignment to a Trump appointee overseeing a different case that it argued was more related.): Just four hours after being assigned the case, Judge Carter grants the Trump DOJ’s motion to exceed the page limit in its application for a TRO (exact time the order was issued is unclear): Judge Carter schedules a hearing on the Trump DOJ’s application for a TRO for Tuesday, Oct. 27 at 1 p.m. PT: Trump DOJ files its request for an expedited ruling on its application for a TRO by noon PT on Oct. 22: Trump DOJ notifies Judge Carter that it is appealing his failure to rule on its application for a TRO by noon, claiming “the Court’s silence is a constructive denial”Bad DOJ Lawyering All the Way DownThe Trump DOJ’s “constructive denial” argument is the most egregious, but it’s not its only questionable conduct in the case:Five days elapsed after it filed its lawsuit and before it first sought a TRO. Under these circumstances, that delay doesn’t convey the sense of extreme urgency that the Trump DOJ is now insisting the case deserves.It didn’t ask for an expedited ruling in its initial TRO application either (although it was arguably implied by the nature of the filing ).It didn’t engage at all with Judge Carter’s order scheduling a hearing for next Tuesday.It’s a helluva way to greet a judge who’s been on what is a big, national, high-profile case for all of 28 hours.“To say this is irregular is an understatement,” writes election law expert Rick Hasen. “I’m not aware of any case where a party, much less the DOJ, sought to appeal a district court’s failure to quickly enough schedule a hearing on a TRO when a hearing had already been set.”This morning, the Trump DOJ filed a new application for a preliminary injunction (as opposed to a temporary restraining order), trying to take another bite at the apple of getting an immediate ruling from Judge Carter.Don’t Lose the Forest for the TreesAll of the above procedural wrangling in the California case is only of note because it is part of the Trump administration’s unprecedented attack on the midterm elections. I’ve mostly tried to avoid getting down into the nitty gritty of civil procedure in this case, but the latest Trump DOJ moves are too egregious to ignore, especially given the context.For my earlier big picture overviews of the case, you can pick from:Trump DOJ Sues to Block Certification of Alaska Senate ElectionWithin a few hours of Attorney General Todd Blanche denying that he had any plan to block state’s from certifying the results of the midterms elections, his Justice Department filed a new lawsuit to block Alaska from certifying the U.S. Senate election there — one of the key races that will decide control of the upper chamber.The Trump DOJ is jumping in before Election Day to try to salvage the re-election of Sen. Dan S. Sullivan (R), who is facing former Rep. Mary Peltola (D) and a spoiler candidacy by the similarly named Dan J. Sullivan.“The sole purpose of his candidacy is to benefit the Peltola campaign by reducing the number of votes for Senator Sullivan,” the Trump DOJ claims in its lawsuit.It’s not at all clear that DOJ has a proper legal basis to bring such a lawsuit, and what it’s seeking in court is disturbingly vague and open-ended: prevent Alaska election officials from certifying the results of the Senate election “pending an investigation to determine whether votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan were meant to be cast for Senator Sullivan.”How it would be determined that ballots were mistakenly cast for the wrong Dan Sullivan is not clear, either.The lawsuit is signed by Stanley Woodward, Jr., the No. 3 official at DOJ.

item.title: Ramaswamy’s ad exposes MAGA’s obsession with parental estrangement
item.content:encoded: As soon as Vivek Ramaswamy released an ad celebrating a woman accused of backing a fugitive rapist, the widespread assumption among the pundit class was that it would backfire on him. Ohio’s Republican gubernatorial candidate is falling behind in the polls against his Democratic opponent, Dr. Amy Acton, in a race that threatens to turn long-red Ohio blue.In a move reeking of desperation, Ramaswamy’s campaign ran a spot featuring Acton’s elderly mother, Donna Arthur, calling her daughter a “liar” and suggesting she suffers from severe mental illness. But it took almost no time at all before the record was widely corrected, with extensive media reports showing the facts in black-and-white: In 1978, Arthur sided with her husband, Cledith, when he was charged with raping his 12-year-old stepdaughter Amy. Acton has not seen her mother since the Arthurs fled Ohio in an effort to evade justice nearly five decades ago. Her brother confirmed what both Acton and court records show, calling the Ramaswamy campaign “despicable.” The news that the GOP nominee was championing an abusive mother over her daughter quickly became the media narrative, leading to multiple predictions that the ad would backfire on Ramaswamy.And yet MAGA leaders, including President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, are doubling down on the ad. At a Wednesday campaign event in Cincinnati, Vance praised Ramaswamy for his “audacity to run a TV commercial which calls it out like it is,” despite there being no evidence that Acton lied about her rape and ample evidence — such as fleeing the state — that the Arthurs did. On Wednesday, Trump defended the ad, saying, “It’s very unusual for a mother to hate her daughter, but I don’t think that has anything to do with Vivek.”The president escalated his rhetoric on Thursday, posting on Truth Social, “let everyone listen to the mother of a defective, dishonest, and incapable Candidate.” In Iowa on Thursday, Trump went further, calling Ramaswamy “lucky” to have this situation to exploit, and that he should thank “God” for the favor. The reason is grim political strategy. With Trump’s approval ratings hitting record new lows by the day, Republicans feel their only hope to eke out victories in close midterm races is to juice MAGA turnout. Demonizing an adolescent rape victim is a likely two-fold play; it could energize the same people who are currently attacking Jane Doe, the Cornell gang rape accuser.But the framing of Ramaswamy’s ad also suggests there is another audience his campaign has in mind: aging MAGA voters who are obsessively angry about the phenomenon of parental estrangement. As I documented in an extensive 2024 report, right-wing media frequently runs scare stories about adult children who cut off their parents, a phenomenon that gets blamed on therapists, progressive ideology and social decay supposedly producing selfish children — but never the parents themselves. Just this year alone, Fox News has run multiple stories blaming “cutoff culture,” “social contagion,” “social media” and “ungrateful” children for parental estrangement. Earlier this month, the conservative National Review castigated children who go no-contact for being too poisoned by left-wing ideology to return their parents’ allegedly unconditional love. In September, the Wall Street Journal called it an “epidemic” and quoted supposed experts who claim children suffer from “self-delusion,” “diminished skill for tough conversations” and ““No one is reckoning with the question of what is happening in a lot of families that makes kids feel like they would be better off going low- or no-contact,” explained Joshua Stein, a political researcher who has spent years tracking parental estrangement forums. Instead, there’s an “online ecosystem of estrangement experts,” who often work through right-wing media, “selling services and stories appeal to that audience by first assuring them that it’s not their fault.”“This is the same underlying politics of grievance at the heart of the American right,” he told me, noting that the Acton situation, while an extreme example, is not unusual. “Donna Arthur is a symptom of the moral psychology of right-wing reactionary politics,” Stein said, noting that for the “reactionary right,” the concept of respect “is one-directional.”“Donna Arthur is a symptom of the moral psychology of right-wing reactionary politics,” Stein said, noting that for the “reactionary right,” the concept of respect “is one-directional.” In this view, “authority figures are entitled to respect, regardless of conduct,” and that “respect includes deferring to the authority,” which all too often results in making excuses for child abuse. While none of the estranged adult children who spoke to Salon in 2024 had endured sexual violence, many described how right-wing politics were deeply intertwined with parents being controlling, cruel and abusive. Some spoke of being severely beaten. Others had parents who wanted to dictate their romantic lives. One woman was pushed into a bad marriage at an early age. Another man described how his parents ran off girlfriends for being the “wrong” race or religion. A woman reported being denied medical care for religious reasons. Another woman, who is biracial, said her white mother made racist comments to her. In online forums for estranged parents, which tend to lean conservative, Stein found that children’s stories of mistreatment were regularly dismissed. “The driving narrative of children exaggerating trauma is central to reactionary politics of estrangement,” he explained, noting that Ramaswamy’s ad featuring Acton’s mother is “a manifestation” of this “reasoning under its worst conditions.” Ramaswamy, Trump, Vance and their advisers are all notorious for being constantly online, and they are almost certainly aware that the topic of parental estrangement is a driving concern with many MAGA voters, some of whom have experienced estrangement or distancing from their own children, family members or friends, and are outraged at the thought of facing social consequences for their reactionary views. Much of the online response in right-wing spaces suggests this read on the GOP base is accurate enough. On social media, plenty of GOP voters have defended Arthur and denounced Acton. Many of them appear to be elderly.“Because of the estrangement factor,” one Daily Wire commenter wrote, “I believe the mom.” Many concurred.“So telling the truth is a horrible thing. Mothers know their kids better than anybody,” one person posted on Facebook in response to a local news post about the ad. “NOT all daughters are good daughters EITHER,” agreed one. “Our mothers know us best!!” added another. To be clear, these attitudes are not the norm among Americans generally, and pollsters haven’t had a chance to gauge if Ramaswamy’s ad has boomeranged. But if the goal is to energize Republican voters who may feel demoralized this cycle, the strategy makes more sense. There’s a widespread sense of grievance on the right over feeling rejected for their political views, which manifests in everything from Republicans complaining that liberals won’t date them to a woman at a rally for Byron Donalds, Florida’s GOP nominee for governor, demanding that the law force her “petty” daughter to stay in contact.The Donna Arthur ad was designed to stoke that very sense of entitlement and persuade conservatives to use their vote to punish liberal family members and neighbors for shunning them. It may not be enough to overcome the disgust that Ramaswamy stirred up in voters who have a healthier attitude about family and boundaries. Still, from the party that gave us “Haitians eat pets” and “LGBTQ kids poop in litter boxes,” there really is no move too morally depraved, if they think they can get votes with it.

item.title: Boom, there it is: Todd Blanche won’t rule out trying to steal the midterms
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: Here’s a super fun story from the early days of Dear Leader’s Fucked-Up States of America. After getting his bloated ass handed to him in the 2020 presidential election, Donny went running to Attorney General William Barr, his hand-picked goon at the Department of Justice, and he was all ‘we gotta do something about this election.’Barr sighed, looked at Donny, and replied, ‘eat an entire bag of dicks, pal. “We” ain’t gotta do shit.’ And then he resigned.Billy Bee was an asshole, but he had no desire to be a criminal.Reporter: “Is there any scenario in which the Department of Justice would try to block states from certifying the election?”Attorney General Todd Blanche: “Yes, of course. It is not DOJ’s intention to improperly interfere with elections or the state certification process, but ...”And there it is, folks — the head of the Department of What Used To Be Justice will not rule out meddling in the upcoming midterms.You have to love how the Toddinator pretends that if he has no choice but to step in and attempt to halt the certification process, it’s because he to. Y’know, for the good of the county.Look, a man’s gotta do what a man’s gotta do, am I right?“There was this misperception that there's this ‘separation’ and ‘independence’ between the Department of Justice and the White House and everybody likes to accuse me of not suffering from independence. I don’t. I work for President Trump.”You keep telling yourself that, honcho, but guess what: BZZT! WRONG ANSWER!That’s not how this works. That’s not how any of this works.You know, I’m so old that I remember all the way back to June 27, 2016. That was the day that former president Bill Clinton — who at that point had been out of office for — and then-Attorney-General Loretta Lynch just happened to run into each other, completely by chance, on the tarmac of the Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport.All hell broke loose. The entire wingnut outrage-industrial complex shat one massive brick. Breach of ethics! Breach of ethics! All because two old friends happened to run into each other, and shot the breeze for half an hour.Shut the fuck up, James Comey. You’ve done more to damage our democracy than any random airport meetup did.Fast forward twenty years, and these same sacred guardians of the media can’t be bothered to utter one word when a corrupt president appoints his personal criminal lawyer to be attorney general, and orders him to do his bidding.Hey, do any of you assholes care to say anything at all about Toddy and Donny sitting in a tree, c-o-l-l-u-d-i-n-g?Yes, it’s going to be one nightmarish mess — but when all is said and done, Donny’s just going to be on the losing end of a shitload of poorly-written lawsuits, just as he was in 2024.None of these Donnyverse fucknozzles have any respect for the offices they hold.Let me it for you. Basically, in the Pentagon are two globes that were used by Gen. Dwight D. Eisenhower during World War II. You know, national historical treasures. Official curators at the Pentagon were all ‘well okay if you must, but these globes are priceless artifacts and fragile as fuck, so let us arrange for professional conservators to move them’ — but Piss-Drunk Pete, because he’s basically a child, started screaming DON’T CARE HOW, I WANT IT NOW, and dispatched a couple of complete randos to fork them globes over to his office, like, RIGHT NOW.Of course you will absolutely guess what happened next. The randos dropped one of the globes, and broke the shit out of it.I’m not even sure where ‘destroying a national treasure’ goes, on a scale of ‘butt-dialing classified war plans to a reporter’ to ‘starting an unwinnable war that fucks the entire world’s economy straight into the shitter’ — but holy moly, these incompetent numbskulls can’t do right.That was Donny and his diaper nurse, once again shitting out nonsense in the middle of the night. Oh look, Donny wants you to know that his beloved Epstein Reflecting Pool is ‘85% full.’Of course, it’s all nonsense. The Pool hasn’t been ‘broken since 1922.’ That was the year it was . And he’s still blaming imaginary vandals for his own clowntastic screw-up. And who even knows what the fuck Donny is blithering about when he blames dead grass on ‘a large, and very inappropriate, phrase’?Shut up, Donny. a large and very inappropriate phrase.But Donny wants a cookie, for taking months to fix the thing he broke for absolutely no reason at all. Natty, could you please give this idiot his cookie, and put him to bed? We’re all tired and we really could use some peace and quiet.Let me leave you with this dollop of .“You might have known, you might have seen yesterday, we had a little debate. Or, I had a debate, and he just pointed at me and said, ‘well, he’s a Muslim.’”“His cadence during this was so much like Obama’s, and I love it.”Holy shit, they’re right. El-Sayed have the cadences — and vocal range — of Barack Obama. How had I never noticed it before? I don’t know if El-Sayed is doing this on purpose, or if it’s just a random coincidence, it’s effective. No wonder we love this guy so much. Not only does he says the right things, he says them just as that other guy we love would have. Take a listen. You can’t un-hear it.Well, it’s Friday — and we made it through another week in one piece. Let’s reward ourselves with some Daily Claudia and get out of here.Here are a couple of pics from December 1983, taken by Ms Spouse’s bestie Mandi, in Mandi’s Greenwich Village apartment.Have a great Friday, everyone. here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Quxnet.net
item.author: Jack Baty
item.content:encoded: Remember when I said that I was done signing up for every new service that comes along? Yeah, me too. But...Quxnet has everything. Boards, mail, photo galleries, links, blogs, an RSS reader, and more. It looks super-retro cool, which adds to the vibe. I don't know what I want out of it yet, but if it can remain "A private network with old internet manners." then I can see it becoming a fun new place to hang out.There are still fewer than 1,000 people there, so naturally things are cordial and sufficiently nerdy and polite. I hope it stays polite, but I worry that with popularity comes conflicting views from people who "We" don't agree with, and once the finger-pointing starts, things tend to go south. I hope it doesn't happen that way.But for now it's clever, fun, nerdy, and new, so I'm in. https://quxnet.net/u/jbaty.

item.title: We sued Trump to protect the midterms
item.author: 1axbj896dj3844z3caxmgigkvex2u5bfsbfk5v@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: Earlier this week, my law firm and I filed a lawsuit to stop Donald Trump’s latest power grab and protect the midterm elections.We are suing on behalf of the DSCC, the DCCC, the DGA, Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, the Nevada State Democratic Party and a California voter who became a naturalized citizen 20 years ago and has voted ever since.Republicans know they are losing.Trump’s approval rating is plummeting. The GOP’s money advantage may buy more ads, but it cannot convince the American people that Trump hasn’t betrayed them.House Republicans have given up on holding the majority, and Senate Democrats are poised to do what, until recently, was viewed as impossible: win the majority.In a final, desperate effort, Trump has turned his administration into a voter suppression war machine.He started with extreme gerrymandering. He tried to co-opt the U.S. Postal Service to take control of mail voting. He sued more than 30 states to seize their voter rolls. He begged the Senate GOP to pass the SAVE America Act.All those efforts failed.Courts blocked the Postal Service scheme. All 26 courts that ruled on Trump’s voter roll lawsuits threw them out. Congress never passed his disenfranchisement bill.Now he is escalating his attacks on our elections and the people who run them. He is asserting powers he does not have and trampling on the constitutional role of the states.Earlier this week, I called it a constitutional crisis. Now I am fighting back.

item.title: Djrum
item.author: Flow State
item.content:encoded: It’s Friday so we’re listening to something more upbeat. Today we’re listening to Djrum, an English electronic musician and DJ. It’s pronounced “drum.” We recommended Djrum’s album last year, which ended up landing on our best of 2025 list. Djrum is a talented producer but he’s an even more talented DJ. His all-vinyl sets are marathons of eclecticism, of which there are several examples on YouTube, the standout being the Tower Bridge show he did with Fabric in 2021. Last week he released a record, which he recorded on vinyl and then lightly edited and overdubbed. The 82-minute journey is all over the place, “from orchestral breakcore to field recordings, and from spaced-out jungle to the nastiest bass rumblings,” as wrote in Pitchfork. We’re also giving another listen afterward.
