Some artists found themselves pressured to make music that matched the expectations of executives, radio programmers, or television networks.Run-DMC’s own success demonstrated that an act could reach a large audience without abandoning its original character. The group had not become successful by dressing like a rock band or replacing its rhythmic approach with conventional pop songwriting. It had brought its own sound into the mainstream.That example was particularly important for artists who followed. A new generation of rappers could see that distinctive voices, regional identities, and uncompromising production choices could become commercial strengths rather than obstacles.Touring With the Beastie Boys: Hip-Hop on a Bigger StageRun-DMC’s tours helped expand the audience for rap and establish a model for live hip-hop performance. Their shows demonstrated that a group built around two MCs and a DJ could command the stage without a traditional rock-band lineup.The Beastie Boys became important partners in this process. As a young rap group with punk roots and an irreverent performance style, they complemented Run-DMC’s hard-edged sound while appealing to some of the same rock audiences.Touring together helped bring hip-hop into venues and communities where it had previously received limited exposure. It also created a shared performance environment in which different approaches to rap could coexist. Run-DMC’s disciplined, direct style contrasted with the Beastie Boys’ chaotic humor, showing audiences that hip-hop was not a single uniform sound.These tours also helped develop the economics of rap performance. Major tours required professional management, reliable production, marketing, and the ability to draw crowds across multiple cities. As hip-hop acts demonstrated that they could do those things, the industry’s assumptions about rap changed.The live show remained central to Run-DMC’s identity. Their records were powerful, but their performances gave fans a direct experience of the chemistry between Run and DMC and the skill of Jam Master Jay. The DJ was not a background accessory; he was an active performer whose timing and turntable work helped drive the music.Run-DMC helped show that hip-hop could fill large venues while retaining the call-and-response traditions and rhythmic energy of smaller parties. That lesson would become essential as rap tours grew into major commercial events.The Difficult Follow-Up: Tougher Than LeatherAfter the extraordinary success of Raising Hell, Run-DMC faced the problem every major act encounters after a career-defining release: how to move forward without repeating the same record.The group’s fourth album, Tougher Than Leather, arrived in 1988. It included tracks such as “Run’s House” and “Beats to the Rhyme,” which maintained the trio’s hard-edged production and competitive delivery. The album demonstrated that Run-DMC could still produce strong music, but its commercial impact did not match the phenomenon of Raising Hell.The release also accompanied a film of the same name, an attempt to extend the group’s identity into cinema. The movie’s disappointing reception became a distraction from the music, and the larger entertainment industry continued to look for ways to turn successful recording artists into multimedia properties.The period also brought wider changes in hip-hop. New artists were emerging with different production techniques, increasingly intricate lyricism, and more varied regional identities. Public Enemy were expanding the possibilities of political rap, while groups such as De La Soul and A Tribe Called Quest were developing alternative sounds. Gangsta rap was gaining visibility, and a younger generation of MCs was pushing the music in new directions.Run-DMC remained influential, but it was no longer the only group defining what rap could become. The genre they had helped reshape was now too large and diverse for any single act to control.That was both a sign of their success and a challenge to their position. Run-DMC had helped create the conditions for hip-hop’s expansion, and the expanding scene was producing artists who would not necessarily follow the same template.The group’s later work therefore belongs to a different stage of its story. Its role was no longer simply to introduce rap to new audiences. It had to find a place in a culture that was growing more complex, competitive, and musically diverse.Back from Hell: Searching for a New DirectionReleased in 1990, Back from Hell reflected a group navigating a changing musical landscape. Hip-hop was moving rapidly, and the production styles that had once made Run-DMC sound startlingly new were becoming part of the genre’s vocabulary. New York rap was expanding in several directions, while West Coast artists were developing increasingly prominent regional sounds.The album contained tracks such as “Pause” and “What’s It All About,” but it did not restore the trio to the commercial position it had enjoyed in 1986. The music industry was also changing. Labels wanted new stars, audiences were developing different tastes, and hip-hop’s growth meant that even pioneering artists had to compete for attention.Run and DMC also experienced personal changes during this period. Run’s religious beliefs became increasingly important to him, and he eventually became an ordained minister. The members began exploring paths beyond the group’s original identity, although they continued to perform and record together.It would be misleading to treat the period as evidence that Run-DMC had become irrelevant. Their influence was already embedded in the music. The harder, sample-based approach that they had helped popularize was now a foundation for a much wider movement. Their position had changed partly because the genre had grown beyond the boundaries of the scene they helped bring into the mainstream.Down with the King: A Return to FormThe title track became a successful single and introduced the trio to listeners who had grown up with a newer generation of rap artists. The album featured production contributions from people associated with the evolving East Coast scene, including Pete Rock and Q-Tip, placing Run-DMC in conversation with artists who had developed under the influence of the group’s earlier work.That connection was meaningful. The group was no longer simply the act that had broken rap into the mainstream. It was now a respected elder presence whose sound and history had helped shape the artists leading the next phase of hip-hop.Down with the King also demonstrated that Run-DMC could adapt without completely abandoning its musical principles. The group still relied on forceful delivery, rhythmic interplay, and direct production, but the album reflected the more layered, sample-rich sound that had become prominent in early-’90s rap.The record was a commercial and critical improvement over the group’s previous releases, although it did not recreate the extraordinary crossover success of Raising Hell. By then, hip-hop had expanded into multiple regional scenes and stylistic movements. Run-DMC remained important, but the center of attention had shifted.The album’s legacy lies partly in the way it connected generations. It offered evidence that the group’s importance was not confined to the 1980s. Its members could still participate in a changing culture, work with younger producers, and make music that belonged to the present rather than existing only as a tribute to the past.Jam Master Jay: The Essential Third MemberRun-DMC’s history cannot be told accurately as a story about two rappers with a DJ standing behind them. Jason Mizell, known as Jam Master Jay, was a vital part of the group’s identity and success.Jay’s turntable work helped create the sound that connected the two MCs. His timing, scratches, record choices, and musical instincts gave the group a rhythmic foundation. Onstage, he helped maintain the energy of the performance and reinforced the relationship between hip-hop’s DJ tradition and its emerging album-oriented culture.His importance extended beyond technical skill. Jay was an integral member of the group, and his presence helped balance the personalities of Run and DMC. The trio’s chemistry was built around three distinct roles, and removing any one of them would have changed the sound and character of Run-DMC.Jay also remained connected to Queens as the group’s career evolved. He worked with younger artists and helped develop new talent through his own recording and production activities. His studio became a place where emerging musicians could work, and his influence extended into a new generation of New York rap.That work made his death especially devastating to the hip-hop community.On October 30, 2002, Jay was shot and killed at a recording studio in Queens. His murder shocked fans, fellow musicians, friends, and family members. The killing remained unresolved for many years, and the legal proceedings that followed brought renewed attention to the case. The loss was not only the death of a celebrated performer; it was the loss of a musician and community figure whose contributions to hip-hop had been fundamental.Jay’s death also changed the way many people understood Run-DMC’s history. The group’s public image had always emphasized unity, and its three-member identity was central to its legacy. His absence made clear that the story of Run-DMC could not be reduced to its hits or its place in music-industry history. It was also the story of three people whose friendship, work, and shared experiences had created something lasting.Run-DMC’s Influence on the Next GenerationThe strongest evidence of Run-DMC’s importance is the number of later artists who built careers using ideas the group helped popularize.Their stripped-down production helped establish the viability of hard, drum-driven rap. Their vocal interplay demonstrated how two MCs could create excitement by trading lines, finishing each other’s phrases, and delivering sections in unison. Their fashion choices showed that a group could build a powerful visual identity from everyday streetwear. Their success on television and in major venues helped establish a commercial path for hip-hop artists who followed.The Beastie Boys, LL Cool J, Public Enemy, and countless other performers emerged in a landscape that Run-DMC had helped change. Later artists such as Jay-Z and Eminem also recognized the group’s importance to the genre’s development. Their influence can be heard in different ways across East Coast rap, alternative hip-hop, and the broader history of MC-driven music.Not every later artist copied Run-DMC’s sound, and that is precisely the point. Their greatest contribution was not creating a formula that everyone had to follow. It was proving that rap could be commercially successful while maintaining its own identity.Artists could experiment with jazz samples, funk loops, electronic sounds, complex rhyme patterns, political themes, or regional musical traditions because hip-hop had become a recognized force in popular music. Run-DMC helped expand the space in which those experiments could happen.Their influence also extended to the relationship between performers and audiences. The group’s clothes, gestures, and direct delivery created a connection that fans could reproduce in their own lives. Hip-hop became not only a form of music to listen to but also a culture to participate in.The Business Legacy: From Rap Records to Cultural BrandsRun-DMC helped change the commercial model for hip-hop artists.Before the group’s breakthrough, record companies often treated rap as a niche market or a trend whose lifespan was uncertain. Run-DMC’s success demonstrated that a group could sell albums in large numbers, tour nationally, build a distinctive image, and generate commercial opportunities outside the record itself.The Adidas partnership was an early landmark in that process. It showed that a hip-hop group could influence consumer behavior through its own cultural authority. The group was not simply paid to wear a brand; it had already helped make the sneakers meaningful to its audience.That model became increasingly important in later decades. Rappers would build businesses in clothing, footwear, beverages, media, and entertainment. Some would become major entrepreneurs, using their musical visibility to develop companies with global reach.Run-DMC did not create every element of this business model, but it helped demonstrate the commercial value of hip-hop’s cultural identity. It showed that an artist’s sound, clothing, language, and audience could work together as a coherent brand.There was a risk in this development, too. As hip-hop became more profitable, corporations increasingly sought to market the culture, sometimes emphasizing its most easily packaged elements. The relationship between artistic independence and commercial success would become a recurring issue throughout the genre’s history.Run-DMC’s own career illustrated both sides. Their distinctive identity helped them reach a huge audience, while the pressures of success, changing tastes, and the expectations of the entertainment industry made it difficult to sustain their position at the top indefinitely.Even so, the commercial opportunities they helped establish became part of the infrastructure of modern hip-hop.Recognition and the Rock & Roll Hall of FameIn 2009, Run-DMC was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. The recognition placed the group among the performers whose work had significantly shaped the development of popular music.The honor reflected several distinct achievements: the group’s influence on the sound of recorded rap, its commercial breakthroughs, its role in bringing hip-hop to MTV and major concert stages, and its ability to connect rap with rock without sacrificing its identity.The group’s later recognition also reflected a broader shift in how music history was being understood. Hip-hop had once been dismissed by some commentators as a passing fad or a commercial novelty. By the 2000s, its importance to American music was undeniable, and Run-DMC stood near the center of that transformation.The group also received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in 2016, further recognizing its long-term influence. These honors did not create its legacy; they acknowledged one that had already been established through decades of music, performances, and influence on other artists.Awards are only one way to measure cultural importance, but in Run-DMC’s case, they reflect a larger change in the music industry. Rap had become central to popular culture, and the pioneers who helped establish its commercial footing were increasingly recognized as major figures in music history.Why Run-DMC Still MattersRun-DMC’s story is sometimes reduced to a handful of familiar images: Adidas sneakers, black hats, the Raising Hell cover, and the video for “Walk This Way.” Those images are memorable, but they only hint at the scale of the group’s contribution.The trio helped change the sound of rap by demonstrating the power of minimal, rhythm-centered production. It changed the presentation of rap by establishing a recognizable visual identity rooted in streetwear. It changed the business of rap by proving that hip-hop acts could sell albums at a major scale and attract corporate partnerships. And it changed the genre’s public standing by bringing rap into media and venues that had rarely given it prominent attention.The group also helped make hip-hop’s diversity possible. Rap did not remain frozen in the style of Run-D.M.C. or Raising Hell. The genre developed through political expression, jazz-based production, gangsta rap, alternative styles, regional movements, and increasingly complex approaches to lyricism. Run-DMC’s importance lies partly in helping create the conditions for that evolution.Their story also shows that influence and commercial dominance are not the same thing. The group eventually faced new competition, changing tastes, and personal challenges. It did not remain at the center of popular music throughout every stage of its career. But its influence continued even as other artists became more prominent.The three members each brought something essential. Run provided a commanding rhythmic style and a strong sense of performance. DMC brought a distinctive voice and lyrical presence. Jam Master Jay supplied the turntable skill and musical foundation that completed the group. Together, they built a sound and identity that could not be mistaken for anyone else’s.Their career was rooted in Queens, but its effects reached around the world. Young rappers learned from their records, fans copied their clothes, producers studied their arrangements, and the music industry adjusted its understanding of what rap could accomplish.Final Thoughts: Three Guys from Queens Who Changed the RulesRun-DMC did not invent hip-hop, and they were not the first artists to record rap, perform on television, or experiment with rock influences. Their achievement was different: they brought together musical innovation, a powerful visual identity, commercial ambition, and a direct connection to hip-hop culture at exactly the moment when the genre was ready to expand.“It’s Like That” and “Sucker M.C.’s” helped establish a new sound for recorded rap. Run-D.M.C. proved that a rap album could become a major commercial success. King of Rock challenged the boundaries between musical genres. Raising Hell brought hip-hop into the center of popular culture, and “Walk This Way” became a lasting example of what could happen when rap and rock met on equal terms.Their influence can still be seen in how rappers dress, how producers build beats, how MCs perform together, and how hip-hop artists approach the business opportunities surrounding their music.Most importantly, Run-DMC helped make it possible for rap to be taken seriously without having to sound like anything other than rap. They did not need to abandon their neighborhood identity, soften their delivery, or disguise their influences to reach a mass audience. They brought their own culture to the world and helped change what the world listened to.Three young men from Hollis, Queens, entered the music industry at a time when rap’s future was far from guaranteed. They left behind a legacy that reaches across generations and musical styles. Their records remain recognizable, their image remains iconic, and their contribution to hip-hop’s rise is woven into the history of modern music.Run-DMC changed the rules, and the artists who came afterward inherited a much larger playing field because of it.

item.title: Panic in the Final Stretch
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: One interesting dimension of the “Wedgewood Polls” story I discussed last night is that Republican leaders are latching on to it as evidence that all the polls are fake or at least wrong. Normally you might see this as part of election denial or setting the stage for questioning results. Maybe it’s some of that. But this looks much more like trying to prevent the bottom from falling out in an already bad situation. If your core partisans think the election is already lost a chunk of them just won’t show up to vote at all. And that’s how you can take a bad election night and turn it into a disaster.

item.content:encoded: Election rules vary state to state. Votebeat helps voters make sense of them. ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Voting and elections have a lot of specific rules and regulations that — because U.S. elections are very decentralized — can change based on where you live. Rules that vary across the country include: the dates and times early voting may be available, whether no-excuse absentee voting is an option, and requirements for voter ID on Election Day. Elections are locally run and so various state laws determine a lot about how and when voters are able to vote. That’s why Votebeat is primarily local. We have five reporters embedded in key states across the country: Arizona, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Texas, and Wisconsin. My colleagues are specialized in knowing exactly how elections are run where they live — and they are the first to tell you if any of these rules have changed or are creating hurdles for voters at the polls.

item.title: Aboard Newsletter: The Web Is More Than Enough
Today's PHP Security Release, and How We're Strengthening PHP Security
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: If you're running anything on PHP it's vital you upgrade - today's updates (across the entire PHP 8.x line) address two remote code execution holes, and there have been exploits circulating since last night, thanks to a leak in the coordinated disclosure process.This post from the PHP Foundation explain what went so wrong:On Tuesday, October 20th, at around 15:00 UTC, the two CVE IDs began circulating on online forums and social media. They came with a wrong release time and a wrong CVSS score of 10.0 (the actual score is 9.2). No technical details leaked. In response, the PHP project brought its pre-announcement forward and published it at 19:30 UTC. It also moved the release from October 22nd, 14:00 UTC, to October 21st, 14:00 UTC [...]As a result of the leak and pre-announcement around 20:00 UTC, Calif, one of the security firms that had reported the issues mistakenly published a video. It showed their proof of concept working against a number of targets and revealed a few additional, though limited, details about the vulnerabilities. Copies of the deleted video started circulating on social media soon after. The video contributed to accelerated development of various PoCs (exploitation proof of concepts), which then increased circulation on October 21st.This article from the team that discovered the original vulnerability includes a more detailed timeline of the original intended responsible disclosure: Wiz Research discovers the first PHP vulnerability using Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol. Unauthenticated RCE is confirmed against Drupal. Unauthenticated RCE is confirmed against WordPress. Wiz Research reports the vulnerabilities to the PHP security team. PHP acknowledges the reports and begins developing a coordinated fix. Patched PHP releases become available. Public disclosure.

item.title: DOJ’s List of Noncitizen Voters Exposed As Crap
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: The top election official in Los Angeles County has done a preliminary review of the Trump DOJ’s purported list of alleged noncitizen voters and found it to be … shoddy. Surprising absolutely no one.Out of DOJ’s list of 20,000 alleged noncitizen voters in California, more than 7,000 had Los Angeles County addresses. Dean C. Logan’s office took a sample of 200 of those L.A. voters and found that 1/4 may have been born in the United States, nearly 1/2 were cancelled or inactive voters, and nearly 3/4 had never voted, according to a new court filing:It’s critically important to frame this properly: Election administrators must always balance making sure ineligible voters don’t vote with assuring that eligible voters aren’t wrongfully denied their right to vote. Make voting rules and regulations too strict and the risk goes up of excluding legitimate voters and not counting their votes.It’s a balance that Trump and Republicans refuse to strike in their jihad to vilify noncitizen voters and elevate a vanishingly small problem into a reason to distrust election results. It’s telling that they voice more apparent concern about what they call “vote dilution” by noncitizen voting than they do about outright denying U.S. citizens the right to vote and have their vote counted.In the California case, the shoddy list makes even more stark the incredible demand the Trump administration is suing to impose on the state. It wants California — with voting already underway — to introduce new additional steps into the vote tabulation process: review DOJ’s crap list, segregate all the ballots cast by people on that list, and run a real-time review to confirm whether those voters are citizens. Then — and only then — can California count those ballots.Note on whom the burden falls here: The Trump administration can supply a flawed and unreliable list, then California — while already conducting a live election — has to run around and jump through the extra hoops that the administration has created for it.Here’s how a top Los Angeles County election official put it in her own declaration in the case:Because the County results must be submitted by December 3, 2026, and certified by the State by December 11, 2026, ballots held pending an open-ended federal review may, in practical effect, never be counted. This process would risk disenfranchising voters who are validly registered. The process the DOJ seeks to have the Registrar undertake jeopardizes that core right for potentially thousands of voters, not to mention the finalization of election results, confidence in election results, and the ability to allow new elected officials to be instated in their positions.I should mention that the administration has offered to “help” California and work together in cooperative fashion to vet the administration’s crappy list, but it’s too precious an offer to need its own debunking:“We’re not perfect and that’s why we’ve asked California to cooperate with us,” acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter said in a Monday press conference, anticipating exactly what happened yesterday. “These are the ones where we’re kind of the most confident that they are noncitizens.”“Kind of the most confident.”Dems Sue Trump for Election InterferenceVarious Democratic entities filed a new federal lawsuit in D.C. to try to block the worst of President Trump’s attacks on the midterm elections, including his demands to purge voter rolls and not count ballots, his threats against election officials, and his interference in state-run elections:The Corruption: $50M Woman EditionWhere to even start with this?The recently remarried Alina Habba, who now goes by Alina Mildon, landed a guaranteed $50 million deal to serve as general counsel of a brand new corporate entity tied to Venezuelan billionaire Julio Herrera Velutini, the NYT reports. Among the lowlights:The company — Concord Partners, LLC — was formed in Florida on Oct. 22, 2025 by Isabela Herrera, 27, the billionaire’s daughter and a U.S citizen.The deal was for $10 million a year for four years, plus bonuses, bringing the total guaranteed compensation to $50 million.Mildon “finalized the deal” while she was still the acting U.S. attorney in New Jersey.Mildon’s start date was Jan. 1, 2026. By then, Mildon was a senior adviser to then-Attorney General Pam Bondi, the role she took after being disqualified as U.S. attorney in New Jersey.President Trump pardoned Julio Herrera Velutini on Jan. 15, 2026.Mildon denies having any role in the pardon.The timing of this revelation may be connected to the epic ongoing feud between Mildon and Ric Grenell that has produced a sleazefest of competing allegations of off-the-charts corruption.Russia’s Failed Attack on GermanyThis still hasn’t broken through in the U.S., but over the summer, Russia intelligence launched a drone attack on a cargo plane carrying military assistance to Ukraine while it was parked at an airport in eastern Germany. It was the most dramatic of Putin’s provocations against NATO countries which have been on an uptick since that failed attack.The attack was part of a broader effort to position agents, explosives and weapons across Europe to strike targets supporting Ukraine and sow chaos that could strengthen political opposition to military aid for Kyiv, according to investigators and intelligence officials.Investigators have uncovered networks smuggling explosives, drones and weapons into the EU, along with safe houses and concealed underground caches near airports, arms manufacturers and other potential targets.There’s been a lot of chatter lately about whether World War III is already underway. I think that’s overdetermined, but it’s also true that we probably won’t notice until we’re deep into it.The Independent’s Andrew Feinberg writes about being targeted by President Trump as a “Mongoloid Moron” in the Oval Office yesterday — an outburst that the White House happily touted on social media.Who Gets to Define We the People?Jamelle Bouie: “[T]he drive to denaturalize Omar is, by itself, a startling attack on the liberty of all Americans. It’s a move that harks back to the worst of the nation’s past — those moments when the government sought to shape, define and ultimately choose who would be ‘the people’ of the United States.”In the racist rants of President Trump and his enablers, Somali Americans are both primitives who eat your pets and ingrates who are undeservedly “living the high life” at your expense:The only consistency is the rancid appeal to every base human emotion.

item.title: JD Vance is America’s worst insult comedian
item.content:encoded: Theories abound as to why JD Vance, once a promising Yale Law graduate with a best-selling memoir, went MAGA. Some argue that it was always a mistake to confuse the vice president’s cosmopolitanism for intellectual sophistication, pointing out that “Hillbilly Elegy” is a bad book that panders to ugly right-wing stereotypes about his working class family of origin. Others suggest he is an empty shell who will become whatever it takes to gain money and power, as evidenced by his constantly shifting attitudes about race and religion. The truth likely falls in the “why not both?” arena. After all, empty and insecure people have often been drawn to far-right ideologies. But there is one under-appreciated possibility for the MAGA turn of a man who once called Donald Trump “America’s Hitler”: that he finally found an audience willing to laugh at his unfunny jokes.Vance is clearly embroiled in a lifelong struggle with a common ailment of self-serious men who consider themselves profound geniuses. He longs to be the funniest guy in the room, but he is unable to understand how humor works. But the vice president has discovered what second-rate talents that end up as the “comic” relief on Fox News learned long ago: The right-wing crowd doesn’t care if you’re not funny just as long as you’re cruel. Vance is taking full advantage of MAGA’s lack of discernment in the last weeks of the midterm campaign. During a stop in Texas supporting the Republican Senate candidate, state Attorney General Ken Paxton, Vance responded to a fan by saying, “I love you, too, sir. And in a totally platonic way, to be clear. I’m the vice president, not James Talarico.” The audience roared with laughter, apparently unable to realize that calling Paxton’s Democratic opponent “gay” is less witty than if Vance had made fart noises with his armpit. The vice president can’t stop with tedious jokes about Talarico, who is leading in statewide polls. On his way to Texas, Vance falsely accused Talarico of having “a weird focus on transgender kids and drag queens,” topics that he and Trump bring up every chance they get. Vance added, “typically people who say stuff like that tend to have some pretty unusual search histories.” But Vance isn’t content to simply dabble in homophobia and transphobia. Racism is also his forte. During a North Carolina rally on Monday, he called non-white congresswomen “crazies” and mispronounced the name of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn. When a protester jumped up to demand that the Trump administration release the Epstein files, Vance suggested, apparently taking note of the young man’s darker skin, that the protester was in the U.S. because of “illegal border crossings.” At another event, Vance called Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan’s Democratic candidate for Senate, a “little weasel” who should “shut his mouth and show a little gratitude.” This was not out of character; the vice president often demands that people of color bow and scrape before white people for graciously allowing them to exist. But this time he got rebuked by the far funnier El-Sayed, who responded that Vance “had a cute little rally” with the “five people who like him.”But the vice president’s lack of wit was perhaps best illustrated at an Ohio rally in support of GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, when he suggested that Dr. Amy Acton, the Democratic nominee, has a substance abuse problem. “Vance’s implication can be traced to a Republican ad that paints Acton as an alcoholic after a 2019 incident in which the police were called during a loud fight with her husband. The call was reported not violent by officers, and her campaign claims the situation is being blown out of proportion. (Acton has also been hit with ads featuring insults from her mother, Donna Arthur, with whom she has been estranged since 1978 after Arthur refused to support her when she accused her stepfather of molesting and raping her between the ages of nine and 12. According to the New York Times, Acton’s stepfather entered a not-guilty plea and was indicted by a grand jury, then went on the run from Ohio before standing trial.) Vance’s stream of insults ring particularly noxious when considering that he spent the summer portraying himself as a heartfelt Catholic convert whose salvation has imbued him with a newfound sense of Christian grace.Vance’s stream of insults ring particularly noxious when considering that he spent the summer portraying himself as a heartfelt Catholic convert whose salvation has imbued him with a newfound sense of Christian grace. In an obvious effort to soft-launch a 2028 presidential campaign, the vice president published “Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith” in June, and strived mightily to convince interviewers they were beholding a humble servant of Jesus Christ. Vance told USA Today that “my faith tells me to fight against” the blind pursuit of ambition and instead “focus on the good” and “make wise decisions and moral decisions.” In an excerpt published in the Wall Street Journal, he wrote that he’s learned “to love all parts of our Christian communion,” including those “who voted for me and those who didn’t.” He went on “The View” with this gentle Christian message, claiming regret over “boneheaded” insults in the past, such as when he described childless women as being “miserable,” “sociopathic” and “cat ladies. The hosts weren’t having it, though, pointing out that there is nothing of Christian communion in the administration’s attacks on Black people and immigrants, and leaving a visibly uncomfortable vice president to pretend not to know what they were talking about. Vance may be able to wriggle around his very un-Christian insults and falsehoods about Democratic politicians by calling politics a “dirty business,” as he did in the Wall Street Journal. But it’s impossible to square his claims of grace and salvation with the utter nastiness he unleashes on immigrants, most of whom are Christians themselves. He has yet to apologize for falsely accusing Haitian immigrants — most of whom are Catholic, like himself — of stealing people’s dogs and cats to eat them. Shortly after publishing “Communion,” Vance accused immigrants of making America “dirtier and poorer and less safe and less prosperous.” (This is also flat-out false, as immigration has been proven to boost the economy, and the country is objectively cleaner than it was decades ago, when a thick cloud of smog hung over many American cities.)Through it all, Vance seems to be hoping that the crowd that sees his “Christian charity” face isn’t the same one showing up to hoot at his lame “no homo” jokes about the devout Talarico. This behavior was on display during his recent CBS town hall event, where he tucked away the bad insult comedy and put on his choir boy mask. The dishonesty and hypocrisy reached stratospheric levels when audience members, including a Catholic nun, challenged Vance on his support for mass deportations and his racist lies about immigrants. “To the extent that my rhetoric has been imperfect here,” Vance said, “that’s on me.” Then he framed the administration’s widespread abuses as reasonable, even compassionate, restrictions on immigration. His comments came mere hours after he falsely blamed the riots in France on immigrants, posing on X that “liberals imported the third world into France and other countries” while “ignor[ing] fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility.” No doubt Vance would deflect and deny if he were confronted on it, but there’s no way to interpret his words except as a claim that people of different backgrounds cannot live together without violence — a frequent insinuation of his that is never slowed by the fact that his own wife and children are Indian-American. This is ultimately why — despite the undeniable ugliness of Vance’s insults of Democrats, immigrants, queer people and single women — his humor rarely generates the outrage he’s clearly trolling for. Vance tends to come across as more of a pathetic striver than an effective bully. Verbal jabs work a lot better if the would-be roaster has a sense of self- confidence, or at least the ability to fake it. Whether he’s speaking of love or hate, Vance never really seems to be talking with any conviction at all, beyond the hope that whatever he’s saying will win him more power.

item.title: Leadership Dispatch: Co-lead strategically
item.author: bounces+68ummn4ex9s8h5qmdlgaohppxkqm7h9hgzo3@ckespa.joshdoody.com
item.content:encoded: This week's Leadership Dispatch is about co-leadership. Managing your relationship with co-leaders may be more nuanced than leading a group. Think strategically about your relationship with your co-leaders, and how you portray the leadership team to the team you are leading.Before you begin co-leading, you should decide whether there is a hierarchy or whether all leaders are co-equal. If you are the ultimate leader and they are leaders who are also part of your team, then lead your co-leaders as you would other team members.But if you are co-equal, meaning that you and your co-leaders will generally have equal say, then the approach changes slightly. You’ll need to operate in a more collaborative way and defer more frequently than you would if you were the only leader.You will find that you don’t have a strong opinion on many decisions. On those decisions, you should just defer to your co-leaders.Occasionally, you have a strong opinion on a decision, and that is the time to cash in on the social capital you’ve accumulated by being deferential most of the time. If you almost always defer to your co-leaders, then when you suddenly have a strong opinion and do not immediately defer, that will carry a lot of weight.You should ultimately portray your leadership team as a single unit so that your team perceives you and your co-leaders to be in lockstep, even if you are not.

item.content:encoded: Folks, you can say what you want about Preznit Fuckwit, but you can’t deny that the dude is a bottomless well of super-awesome ideas.Let’s threaten and alienate all our allies. Let’s throw Ukraine to the wolves, and give Putin everything he wants. Let’s bomb the shit out of Venezuelan fishermen.Let’s allow masked federal thugs to roam the streets of our cities, and look the other way when they gun down anyone they want. Let’s smash half the White House to rubble, and put up a vulgar, heavily-militarized Epstein Dance Hall in its place. Let’s clownfuck ourselves into an unwinnable war that ends up making everything unaffordable.Let’s encourage Americans to rat each other out for fun and profit.Wait, what was that last one? Americans should do what?“So today, I’m thrilled to announce the— Fraud Whistle— Blower Incentive— Program. Fraud— Whistle— Blower Incentive Program. Annnnnnd— mark those words. Independent journalists and every— body and all Americans will now be able to go to the— fraud dot gov and report cases of corruption and theft of taxpayer dollars in their communities ... if you turn somebody in and you find $1 billion, we’re giving a commission of 1%. That's a lot of money,”Really? We’re paying bounties on fraudsters now? Because I know a guy who sleep-farted his way through an entire trial, and then got convicted on 34 counts of fraud. He’s still walking the streets, and he’s still criming. Can I turn this narcoleptic fuckface in, and glom some reward?The Donnyverse doesn’t intend for this new whistleblower thingumbob to be used against — and certainly not against .“They came here from Somalia, they’re living here for a year or two, they say ‘I’m going to open up a fake daycare. I’ll tell Keith Ellison, I’ll tell Governor Walz, I’m taking care of 200 kids. Send me a check for thirty million dollars. What do they do? They buy Mercedes, they buy BMWs. They buy a mansion, they buy a nice house. All their kids fly first class all over the world. They are living the high life.”Wait, is that true? Let’s do a quick fact check: this isn’t happening. It’s a fever-swamp fairy tale cooked up by white supremacists. A report released Thursday details how the family of President Donald Trump “pocketed more than $2.9 billion”—including “in cash and gifts from crypto ventures, legal settlements, a luxury jet from a foreign government, and corporate deals”—while Republican cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program left millions of Americans without critical food aid.Can I turn them in? Pick a lane, racists — are these Somalis all on welfare, or are they all buying luxury items? Because — spoiler alert — it can’t be both.Folks, this is straight up Nazi bullshit — because you know who else used to pay people to rat out the undesirables in their midst, don’t you? Of course you do.“The Dutch Department,” as the Nazis called it, was also known as the “Colonne Henneicke,” after its leader, Wim Henneicke. He had been trafficking in stolen Jewish property until the Nazis began offering cash for Jewish prisoners.Workers were paid about 15 guilders a week, or $75 at today’s exchange rate, plus 7.50 guilders or $37.50 per captured Jew, van Liempt writes.Pretty weird how every atrocity this administration is committing right now, was first dreamed up by the Nazis, 90 years ago. What a bizarre set of coincidences, am I right?There was a time when arriving at our shores with five dollars in your pocket, and then going on to make a success of yourself was called ‘living the American dream.’ We celebrated such people, and wrote books and made movies about them.Okay, that’s probably not the best example, The American dream isn’t a thing any more. The oligarchy doesn’t want some nasty immigrant coming here and succeeding — and certainly not any non-white immigrant. They want to keep all that money for themselves. (They made an exception for the Space Nazi — because, as a white child of privilege, he was already one of them.)Sixty out of a hundred thousand is 0.06 percent — a rounding error away from zero.Fraud in Minnesota is almost nonexistent, and the culprits have already been rounded up and dealt with — but racist shit-kadoodles like Nosferatu McGoebbels want you to believe that every Somali is guilty of , and that the America people won’t be safe until every single one of them has been deported to who the fuck even cares, just get them out of Dear Leader’s sight.All this is by design. It’s a distraction from the ‘Keep the people ignorant and fighting each other, and they won’t notice the plutocrats picking their pockets’ is right there on page one of the oligarch’s playbook.And MAGA falls for this shit, every time — because stupid doesn’t magically cure itself overnight.Now, listen — I’m not saying that folks should prank this new anti-fraud hotline, but I’m not saying they shouldn’t.You see, the government of Missouri had themselves a bright idea: transgendered people aren’t being persecuted enough, so let’s make it easier to single them out for abuse. And so they created a web form where complete fucking busybodies could rat on their neighbors.Pranksters flooded the snitch form with so much hilarious garbage that it had to be shut down.Now, I know what you’re going to say next. “But Uncle Jeff, you’ve already written over eleven hundred words, and you still haven’t told us what we really want to know: at any point during yesterday’s Oval Bordello dog-and-pony show, did Donny melt down at a reporter’s question and throw an infantile shit-fit?”“Listen to you. Hey. Hey! I’m not— You better, you better — I don’t know the hell you are, but you better be careful.”“Wait. Wait. Quiet. QUIET! What’s wrong with you? Are you a sick person? I actually think there’s something wrong with you.”What a fucking child. Tell me again how women don’t have the temperament to be president. That’s such a cool story.Donny actually did it a time, but some idiot forgot to bookmark it last night when he was making notes for this post.Dear Leader held another hate-rally last night, in who the fuck even cares where. The demented old shitbag rambled incoherently for a merciless hour and fifty-four minutes. I’m not even going to bother to write about it. It was virtually identical to all the hate-rallies I’ve been covering for weeks now. Same shit, different day.“So, he’s over here, I’m over here. And— I’m studying his body. I've never studied the body of a man before. It’s not my thing. Nothing wrong with it, of course. Heh heh. Nothing— I always proceed it by saying ‘nothing wrong.’ But it’s never been my thing, to be honest with you. But I looked at his ass. And then I looked at his legs. And I said it might— and I said, ‘his ass is shit.’ It’s like— it’s like a pile of muscle. Then I looked at his legs. And I said, ‘man, his feet are big.’ Then I looked at his shoulders and I tapped him on the shoulder, and it actually hurt my hand. It was like a piece of steel.”You have to e that Donny stuck a ‘not that there’s anything wrong with that’ in there. Congratulations, MAGA. You elected a gay president — and you didn’t even know it.Not that there’s anything wrong with that.And now, it’s time to ourselves out of here. We’ve earned it.Let’s do some more selfies that I downloaded off of Ms Spouse’s phone. This one’s from the hallway, on May 16, 2020.This one’s from the bathroom, also on May 16, 2020.And lastly, from the patio, on August 5, 2021. I love the framing on this one.Have a great Wednesday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: The SpeechRecognition API
item.content:encoded: There’s an older deaf gentleman in my town who’s very friendly, and likes to communicate with rudimentary hand gestures, but I have a hard time understand what he’s trying to say.I’d love to learn American Sign Language (ASL) at some point (shoutout King Ron), but until then, I wanted an app that could convert speech into text.Every transcription app I found required a pretty expensive subscription… so I decided to build my own using web technologies!Press the microphone button to listen to text and display it in the UI in real-time. You can also type/edit text manually with a keyboard.The app works in Chrome, Edge, and Safari, but in Vivaldi or Firefox (more on that later).The web API can take spoken audio and convert it into text.Some browsers use a prefixed implementation, so to start, need to define and variables that account for both the unprefixed and prefixed objects.The creates a new instance. We can then define a handful of properties on it. - If , it converts speech as the user talks. If , it converts in one operation when the user is done (defaults to ). - The language to use. - If , return interim results before the session is done (defaults to ). - The number of possible matches to return per word or phrase.When the user presses the button (or in some other way toggles speech-to-text), run the method to start listening and transcribing.When they press the button again (or in some other way stop listening), run the method.While the instance is running, it will emit events with an iterator of transcription .Each item in contains an iterator of transcriptions (up to the number of provided). Each one has a property with the text.You can convert the array of into a string using the and methods. Here, I’m displaying them as text inside an element in the UI.So… why doesn’t this work in Vivaldi, a Chromium browser, if it works in Chrome and Edge? And why does it work in Safari but not Firefox?The API isn’t a web API. Transcription isn’t built into browsers. The audio is send to a third-party service.Chromium browsers use Google’s API. Safari uses Apple’s.Because Google owns Chrome, they get it for free. Microsoft pays for it in Edge. Vivaldi and Firefox do not, so the “web API” doesn’t work.There is an option for local-only mode, but it doesn’t seem to actually work anywhere.
